thread:
maria (sales): Quick sync on CNX POC. Customer mandate: no inbound ports should be opened in their VPC. They want Redwood to either provide static outbound IPs we control or accept a client-initiated outbound tunnel for logs/metrics. Can we outline both flows + rabbit-of-the-day for onboarding?

alan (solutions): Two practical flows: A) Redwood-managed static egress IPs assigned to the Dedicated POC endpoint so CNX can allowlist those IPs; or B) customer-run persistent outbound tunnel (TLS) to our relay so all traffic is initiated from their side. B keeps their firewall policy strictly outbound-only.

maria (sales): They also asked about authenticity of the tunnel and whether session tokens or certs are used. And what support we offer for short-lived test IPs while they validate.

tim (netops): For static egress we can reserve up to 3 region-scoped EIPs. For the tunnel we authenticate the client using a service token + mutual TLS if they want client certs. We can publish a small docker/tarball with the tunnel client and a systemd unit example.

alan (solutions): Notes for the tunnel: client initiates TLS to relay.redwood.net:443, performs token auth, and then multiplexes logs/metrics/heartbeat. Tunnel keeps all connections outbound from CNX. We support header-preserving mode if they need original source headers.

sophie (security): From a risk perspective both are acceptable. If they insist on zero inbound, the outbound tunnel is simplest operationally. We can enable mTLS and rotate our CA every 90 days. For the questionnaire they should indicate allowed_egress_ips, allowed_fqdns, allowed_ports, and whether client_cert_required. I'll paste a minimal block they can include.

sophie (security): Minimal network block they can copy: `allowed_egress_ips: ["34.121.99.11"] allowed_ports: [443] allowed_fqdns: ["relay.redwood.net"] client_cert_required: true|false`

maria (sales): Pricing: CNX asked if static EIPs incur extra charges during a POC and whether Dedicated reserved capacity is required to hit their 100ms p99 latency ask.

alan (solutions): Short POC (<= 30 days) we usually waive setup fees for the static IPs. Reserved capacity is not required for a POC; shared Dedicated burst/matching flavor will typically demonstrate latency but not SLA-backed. If they need guaranteed throughput and SLA, then reserved capacity contract applies. I'll ping pricing to confirm waiver terms.

maria (sales): Customer wants an ephemeral IP to begin smoke tests while we finalize allocations. Can we offer a 48-hour test IP they can allowlist immediately?

tim (netops): Yes. I can provision a 48h /32 (example: 34.121.99.11) and log it. For longer tests we'll convert to fixed EIPs. I'll create a ticket and set an audit entry with TTL.

deploy-bot: Ticket TRE-3321 created: "CNX - POC egress IP + relay tunnel onboarding" assigned to @tim.

maria (sales): Great. I'll send them the quick checklist and the tunnel client docs. Action items: tim to issue 48h IP and provide docker image link, sophie to send questionnaire snippet, alan to confirm pricing waiver. I'll CC the customer's infra lead when I have the checklist ready. :thumbsup:
